audit.why: Cassiopeia owns this from level 2 onward — Maokai stacks health and Sap Magic sustain, neither of which answers ramping magic DoT, and his only engage is a 525-range dash. Consistent with 58.33% over 48 games.

audit.whatIsWrong: Twisted Advance was called 'matchup-defining' and 'the whole green-light system' with no cooldown number, and Nature's Grasp never appeared as a spike at all.
audit.why: Twisted Advance is 14/13/12/11/10s and Nature's Grasp is 130/110/90s at 3000 range. His level-6 spike is the wall, not the root — Cassiopeia has no dash and cannot cross it.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, report[5].t and wants.you[1] now carry 14s; spikes[2].text adds the Nature's Grasp gate.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three places told the reader to stun Maokai 'mid-Advance' or 'as he commits his Twisted Advance'. He is untargetable for the whole dash, so that instruction spends a 120s ultimate into nothing. Also wrote 'Twin Fangs'; the ability is Twin Fang.
audit.why: Riot's Twisted Advance text: he contorts into a mass of moving roots, becoming untargetable and dashing to the target, rooting on arrival. Miasma's grounding stops the cast before it starts, but once it is off, the answer is the arrival frame, not the transit. Separately, Sap Magic's cooldown is reduced each time he casts a spell or is struck by an enemy spell — every Twin Fang Cassiopeia lands accelerates his heal.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text, whys[4] and mid now say 'on arrival' and name the untargetability; spikes[3].text states the Sap Magic acceleration; name fixed to Twin Fang.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nature's Grasp cutting off a champion with no dash was never mentioned.
audit.why: Cassiopeia's only mobility is Serpentine Grace move speed — a 3000-range advancing wall of brambles behind her is a hard retreat cut, which makes Flash a wall answer rather than a damage answer.

edits.before: Petrifying Gaze stuns him as he commits his Twisted Advance root all-in and turns your won trade into a kill.
edits.after: Petrifying Gaze stuns him on arrival — untargetable through Twisted Advance, so fire the cone as he lands, not before.

edits.before: Petrifying Gaze stuns him out of his Advance-into-Bramble-Smash all-in and converts your won trade into a clean kill.
edits.after: Petrifying Gaze stuns him the frame Twisted Advance lands — he is untargetable in transit, so wait for arrival, then chain E.

edits.before: Malignance or early Liandry's plus your Serpentine Grace move speed lets you chain Twin Fangs and shove him under tower at will.
edits.after: Malignance or early Liandry's plus Serpentine Grace lets you chain Twin Fang and shove him in — never past the wave with Nature's Grasp up.

edits.before: His Sapling spam plus passive Sap Magic sustain is the one window he heals your poke off — back off his minion-aura heals and don't fight inside Twisted Advance range until you have W to ground it.
edits.after: Sapling spam plus Sap Magic is his one heal window, and every Twin Fang you land shortens Sap Magic itself — chip him without committing, and never stand inside Twisted Advance's 525 range with W down.

edits.before: Drop W to ground and slow his Twisted Advance so his root engage can't land and he can't reposition out of your poison
edits.after: Drop W under his feet to ground Twisted Advance — a 14s dash he cannot cast inside the cloud, so his root engage never starts

edits.before: This is your lane to own. Ranks in Q and E mean every poison tick refunds Twin Fang's cooldown and mana, so you kite around his Saplings and shred him in any extended trade he can't disengage from. The key trick: when he commits Twisted Advance, drop your W Miasma to ground him so he can't dash out, then burn him down. At 6, hold Petrifying Gaze for his all-in — stun him mid-Advance and your chained E deletes him before Sap Magic heals anything meaningful.
edits.after: This is your lane to own. Ranks in Q and E mean every poison tick refunds Twin Fang's cooldown and mana, so you kite around his Saplings and shred him in any extended trade he can't disengage from. The key trick: drop W Miasma under his feet before he casts, because grounded he cannot Twisted Advance at all — and once it is off he is untargetable the whole dash. At 6, hold Petrifying Gaze for the arrival, not the transit: stun him as the root lands and chained E deletes him.

edits.before: - Maokai Twisted Advance (Root): matchup-defining — Point-and-click root — count its cooldown before stepping up. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget W Miasma for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Maokai Twisted Advance (Root): matchup-defining — 14s at rank 1, and Miasma grounds the cast; once it is off he is untargetable in transit, so R the arrival. - Budget W for his step-up and the 120s R for his commit.

edits.before: Point-and-click root — count its cooldown before stepping up. Bait it, count it, then go.
edits.after: Point-and-click root on a 14s cooldown at rank 1 — count it, bait it, then step up.

edits.before: Track Maokai’s Twisted Advance (Root): Point-and-click root — count its cooldown before stepping up. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Track Maokai’s Twisted Advance: 14s at rank 1. Miasma grounds the cast, but he is untargetable in transit — so stun the arrival, not the dash.

notes: The 'stun him mid-Advance' instruction appeared in three separate fields and would waste a 120-second ultimate — Twisted Advance grants untargetability for the whole dash. All three now say arrival. The packet levelChart is [Skill,Cassiopeia x6] while both on-disk layers read Cassiopeia for all seven rows; I left the chart alone. Only 48 games in the sample, so the win rate is soft.
